I have been farming this 2.6 mu for 20 years, since I was 22. I finished middle school, so I can read the labels on fertilizer bags and do the math for my small field. My husband works construction in the county town, so he is not here for the busy seasons. I do most of the farm work myself, with my mother-in-law helping sometimes. We have four mouths to feed, and the farm income has to cover the inputs.

For my winter wheat on the full 2.6 mu: Last year I planted the improved wheat variety that I bought from the seed shop in town, and I got about 500-something kg per mu. This year I will plant the same improved seed — 7.5 kg per mu. I see no reason to change. Before sowing in October, I will run the rotary tiller to loosen the soil. For fertilizer, I put a base of compound fertilizer, about 50 kg per mu, the kind that says 15-15-15 on the bag, and I add a little extra phosphate because wheat needs strong roots before winter. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I topdress with urea — I will spread about 40 kg per mu. I know that is on the high side, but my neighbor across the road uses about the same, and his wheat always looks greener and fuller than mine. I cannot afford a bad harvest. If I waste 20 yuan on extra fertilizer, that is nothing compared to losing 200 jin of grain. I figure that gives me roughly 25 kg of nitrogen per mu, about 10 kg of phosphorus, and 8 kg of potassium.

I will irrigate the wheat three times: once before winter freezes the ground, once at jointing in spring when it starts shooting up, and once at grain filling in May. The well water is good, but the electric pump costs money, so three times is enough. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once in early spring to kill the weeds, and if I see aphids or rust, I spray once more. That makes two pesticide applications. I expect about 550 kg per mu if the spring weather cooperates.

For summer maize on the same 2.6 mu: Right after wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid maize seed. Everyone around here uses hybrid seed now — the old traditional types cannot compete. I do not till for the maize. There is no time between wheat harvest and maize sowing, and hiring the tractor costs 60 yuan per mu. I sow directly into the wheat stubble. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing, about 50 kg per mu, and then at the big trumpet stage in July, I topdress with about 30 kg per mu of urea. That should be around 22 kg of nitrogen per mu, and about 8 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. I irrigate twice — once at sowing if the soil is dry, and once in late July when the ears are filling. I spray herbicide right after sowing to keep the weeds down, and once more in summer for corn borers. Two pesticide sprays total. If the rain comes right, I expect about 600 kg per mu.

My husband's off-farm wages pay for our daughter's school expenses, but the farm has to feed us and pay for its own inputs. I calculate every bag of fertilizer carefully. I buy from the dealer I trust, and I watch what the neighbors do. If I am not sure, I do what I did last year. Change is risky when you only have 2.6 mu.
